title: Batch/Cache Change Conductor: RBAC Attestation, Staged Apply, Immutable Audit Trail
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Redwood Optimize will suggest batching and KV-prefix caching profiles that can materially reduce token cost for high-throughput text generation workloads. We need a secure, auditable pipeline to apply those configuration changes automatically or semi-automatically without exposing customers to accidental regressions or compliance gaps.

Goal: Build a change conductor that validates recommended batch/cache changes, enforces RBAC/attestation for who can auto-approve or request apply, executes staged applies (dry-run -> canary -> wide rollout), and writes an immutable, signed audit trail for forensics and compliance.

Scope:
- Implement attestation and approver roles for auto-apply and manual apply flows.
- Implement staged apply executor supporting dry-run, 5% canary, 25% ramp, 100% rollout and automated rollback triggers.
- Append-only audit log with cryptographic signatures and KMS/HSM-backed keys; integrate with existing audit retention policies.
- Observability hooks (cost delta preview, token/latency SLO checks) and alerting for regression detection.

Out of scope for this ticket: UI surface changes in Console (separate PM ticket), multi-tenant cross-customer orchestration (handled by Dedicated infra), and matching billing pipeline changes (billing team will be notified separately).

Constraints and non-functional reqs:
- Any auto-apply that changes runtime batching or cache configuration must be revertible within 2 minutes of rollback trigger.
- Audit entries must include pre/post config snapshots, signed assertion of approver identity, and correlation IDs for request traces.
- RBAC roles should map to existing org directory groups (SAML/SCIM) and support temporary elevated access via break-glass with attestation.

Success metrics:
- 90% of suggested cost-optimization changes can be simulated (dry-run) and confidence scored automatically.
- <1% of automated applies result in customer-facing incident (severity >= P1).
- Audit trail tamper-evidence validated in quarterly compliance review.
acceptance_criteria: RBAC: policies defined and enforced for 'optimizer:apply' and 'optimizer:approve' scoped to org/team and environment (hosted/dedicated/private)
Attestation: every non-trivial apply (>= 5% change in batching or cache TTL) has an approver signature or meets configured auto-approve rules and is persisted in audit log
Staged Apply: executor supports dry-run, canary, ramp, and full rollout with ability to pause and automatic rollback on metric breaches
Audit Trail: entries are append-only, include pre/post config, approver identity, timestamp, and KMS-backed signature visible in UI/console and exportable for compliance
Rollback: automated rollback triggers execute and restore previous configuration within 2 minutes for 95% of simulated failure scenarios
Observability: dashboards show cost delta, token latency, error rate and KV cache hit-rate for the affected routes during rollout
E2E tests: integration tests exercising canary failure and rollback paths exist and pass in CI
decisions: Use CloudKMS-backed RSA keys for signing audit entries in hosted, with HSM-backed key option for Private customers
Auto-approve thresholds will be configurable per org and default to conservative values (cost benefit >= 10% and latency delta <= +2%)
Canary percentages hard-coded to 5/25/100 for initial rollout; make percentages configurable in subsequent iteration
Store audit trail in append-only blob storage with signed manifests and a lightweight index in Postgres for searchability
